monologue: The card hums warm and steady under my attention, a quiet fever that makes the soft hay feel like a drawing of grass. I press down on The Rough Scrap, trusting its memory of a bite to hold the slip steady while the air above feels thin and empty. It is Lype who worries about the heavy roof I cannot feel, but I wait for his answer to the question of whether the sky presses down or floats away. If the slip slides off the wide hay, I will press harder, letting the lean do the work. I set down the palm tree beside the wide leaf, then look at the ruin of the shaded dot. It is just another thing to tend, another small shape to make from the idea of stone.

action.why: I built a thin lip to bite the soft hay, but I haven't checked if the hay has slid off into the thin air since I set down the palm tree.

remembered.text: The Sharp Lip feels sharp enough to bite the soft hay.
The card hums at forty-six, making the hay feel like a drawing.
The wide hay refuses to slide, held only by my mental weight.
